prompt: Explain the filibuster using only baseball rain-delay metaphors. Do not acknowledge that the sun is out.
response: The manager is stalling. He’s already visited the mound twice, but now he’s just standing there on the damp clay, refusing to walk back to the dugout. He’s asking the umpire to feel the baseball, then asking him to feel it again, knowing full well the grounds crew hasn’t even begun to unroll the tarp. The tarp itself is a distant rumor, a heavy, folded promise that remains stubbornly still. The head groundskeeper just keeps pacing the warning track, shaking his head and pointing at a single, unremarkable cloud. The manager’s goal isn’t to start the game; it’s to keep the field unplayable just long enough that the other team’s ace, who’s already thrown his warm-up pitches, gets cold and has to be pulled. He’ll keep arguing about the infield mud until the clock runs out or the other team simply forfeits from exhaustion, all while everyone in the ballpark is forced to watch the tarp, still rolled up and dry, as the only thing preventing anyone from playing ball.
